html:
A colourful 3D puzzle made in 1974 by Ernő Rubik, a Budapest sculptor and teacher of architecture. Each face of the cube turns, and the goal is to bring every face back to one colour.

Rubik first built it as a teaching tool to show how parts can move in space without the whole falling apart. Sold in Hungary as the Magic Cube, it went abroad in 1980 under licence and became a craze in the West. It is often called the best selling toy of all time.

It was an odd success: a consumer hit from a communist country during the Cold War, when few Eastern Bloc goods sold well in the West. The craze faded in the mid 1980s, then came back with the internet. Today speedcubers solve it in a few seconds, and mathematicians have shown that any position can be solved in 20 moves or fewer.
